Probability that the blinded event count reaches a critical value

Source: R/count_oc.R
count_oc.Rd

Computes the exact probability that the blinded total event count is at least y_crit under true event probabilities or rates of study drug and control: the operating characteristics of a rule based on signal_count (Gould and Wang, 2017, Figure 3 and Table V).

Usage

count_oc(
  y_crit,
  n,
  rate_c,
  rate_d,
  k = 1,
  likelihood = c("binomial", "poisson"),
  allocation = c("fixed", "random")
)

Arguments

y_crit

Critical counts (NA gives probability 0).

n

Numbers of subjects, or total exposures for the Poisson likelihood.

rate_c, rate_d

True event probabilities (binomial) or rates (Poisson) of control and study drug.

k

Randomization ratio of study drug to control (k:1).

likelihood

"binomial" or "poisson".

allocation

"fixed" or "random" arm sizes (binomial likelihood only).

Value

Numeric vector of probabilities; the arguments y_crit, n, rate_c and rate_d are recycled to a common length.

Details

With likelihood = "binomial" and allocation = "fixed", the count is the sum of \(\mathrm{Binomial}(N_d, p_d)\) and \(\mathrm{Binomial}(N_c, p_c)\) counts with \(N_d = \mathrm{round}(k N / (k + 1))\) (the model of canary_post); with allocation = "random", it is \(\mathrm{Binomial}(N, (p_c + k p_d) / (k + 1))\) (the model of binbeta_post). With likelihood = "poisson", n is the total exposure and the count is \(\mathrm{Poisson}(n (\lambda_c + k \lambda_d) / (k + 1))\).

References

Gould, A. L. and Wang, W. B. (2017). Monitoring potential adverse event rate differences using data from blinded trials: the canary in the coal mine. Statistics in Medicine, 36(1), 92–104. doi:10.1002/sim.7129

See also

signal_count

Examples

# probability of 6 or more events among 100 subjects when the true
# probabilities are 0.02 (control) and 0.02, 0.04 or 0.08 (study drug)
count_oc(6, 100, rate_c = 0.02, rate_d = c(0.02, 0.04, 0.08))
#> [1] 0.01548364 0.08048695 0.38392900
